title: Profiling Chef Recipes: CI pipeline integrations and smoke scripts
content:
Purpose:
This note collects concise, copy-pasteable 'recipes' we can drop into perf CI and small local smoke jobs to produce actionable flamegraphs, annotated traces, and triage artifacts. Aim: reduce friction for engineers to run reproducible profiles and get consistent outputs that plug into the downstream triage/playbooks.

Overview / design decisions:
- Keep CI recipes lightweight: few-second synthetic requests + 10s perf record windows.
- Produce two canonical artifacts per run: a folded flamegraph SVG and a compressed trace bundle (.tar.gz) containing perf.data or eBPF captures and a short metadata JSON.
- Embed run metadata in filename (build, commit, model, sequence_len_bucket) so automation can auto-index.

Quick checklist (copy into CI job step):
1) Warmup: run 2 synthetic requests to warm caches and KV cache.
2) Run collector: perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf -a -o perf.data -- sleep 10
3) Convert: perf script -i perf.data | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
4) Flamegraph: ./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame-<commit>-<bucket>.svg
5) Bundle: tar -czf profile-<commit>-<bucket>.tar.gz perf.data flame-<commit>-<bucket>.svg metadata.txt
6) Annotate: metadata.txt should contain: commit, model, hw-type, seq-len-bucket, sample-rate, ci-job-id

Example GitHub Actions job snippet (minimal):
- name: Run perf smoke
  run: |
    ./scripts/warmup-synth.sh --model bert_small --seq 128
    sudo perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf -o perf.data -- sleep 8
    perf script -i perf.data | ./tools/stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
    ./tools/flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
    tar -czf artifact.tar.gz perf.data flame.svg metadata.txt

Sampling policy catalog (recommended):
- Quick CI: 99Hz, 8-12s window, system-wide (-a), produce flamegraph only. Fast, low cost.
- Deep CI: 199Hz, 30s window, per-container perf + eBPF epoll probes, collect full traces + KV-cache synthetic workload. For weekly runs.
- Local developer: 99Hz, 15s window, optionally run with --no-priv which falls back to perf_user probes.

eBPF hints:
- Use bpftrace one-liners to augment perf when kernel symbolization is missing: trace sched_switch and attach to process PID, capture stack traces for top N PIDs, filter by container id.
- Remember to collect /proc/kallsyms and uname -a for kernel debug.

Triage rubric (after artifact produced):
- Step 0: confirm metadata and reproducibility (model + seq bucket).
- Step 1: open flamegraph, look for broad flat hotspots (syscalls or runtime stalls).
- Step 2: if many context switches -> collect sched and futex metrics; suspect I/O/KV cache contention.
- Step 3: if hot functions in tokenizer or embedding lookup -> verify quantized kernels and check small-batch traces.
- Step 4: escalate to perf-SRE with tarball + brief summary: delta against baseline, top 3 symbols, CPU time percentage.

Naming convention (strict):
profile.<job>-<commit>-<model>-<hw>-<seqbucket>.<ts>.(svg|tar.gz)
example: profile.ci-1428-a2fb9e4-ggml2-gpu32-128-20241101T1423.svg

Failure modes and mitigations:
- perf permission denied: run with sudo in CI runner or use flamegraph-lite eBPF wrapper.
- Unsymbolized frames: include vmlinux and build-id mapping in bundle.
- Noisy baseline: add a baseline artifact per commit that runs on the same runner image and subtract top-k common frames.

Notes / open questions:
- Should CI automatically upload flamegraph SVGs to a lightweight viewer and extract top N symbols into JSON for regression detection? (pros: quick alerts; cons: alert noise)
- Coordinate with observability to ensure token-level sampling events correlate with perf windows for effective KV cache analysis.

Attachments / next steps:
- Draft a small GH Action template in scripts/ci/profiling.yml and a helper script scripts/ci/collect-profile.sh (owner: @Marcus Lee).
- Schedule an async review in #perf-runbooks and iterate on default sampling rates for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Endnotes: this doc is intentionally terse — treat it as a cookbook of drop-in steps rather than a long prose runbook. Add concrete CI job PRs and link them into linked_artifacts so triage tooling can pick them up automatically.
